subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw make gateway-owned shared SQLite access RPC-first/no-maintenance for CLI diagnostics, enforce a broader single-writer lease, or prioritize corruption quarantine before changing live access?
rationale: The source boundary is clear enough to keep the issue open, but the fix changes CLI diagnostics, doctor migrations, gateway ownership, startup/recovery behavior, and data-retention semantics for a persisted shared store.

options.title: RPC-first diagnostic access
options.body: Make health/status/stability ask the running gateway first and allow only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file access while a gateway lease is active.

options.title: Single-writer lease contract
options.body: Have the gateway own write and WAL-maintenance access through an explicit lease, with other processes refusing writer-style shared DB opens while it is held.

options.title: Quarantine-first recovery
options.body: First add preserve/quarantine/fresh-state recovery for malformed openclaw.sqlite, leaving CLI/gateway prevention as a follow-up.

recommendation.title: RPC-first diagnostic access
recommendation.body: Make health/status/stability ask the running gateway first and allow only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file access while a gateway lease is active.

likelyOwner.reason: The database-first refactor and shared SQLite state ownership history make this the best available routing owner for the product boundary choice.
